why: The one PostToolUse handler, field for field. plugin/hooks/hooks.json registers exactly this object under the Edit|Write matcher, so this file is the schema and the committed hooks.json is diffed against it.
provenance: Recorded from the agent-distribution design's hooks.json block and its measured field notes, then reshaped after the harness sweep: Codex 0.156.1, Cursor 2026.09.23, Copilot CLI 1.0.88, VS Code 1.139.0 and Claude Code 2.1.138 all keep `command` and drop `args` and `if`, so the invocation lives in `command` alone. Claude Code ignores a field it does not know rather than refusing it, so a misspelled `asyncRewake` is a hook that runs and never rewakes, silently. A live capture replaces this file and sets `source` to `live-capture`.

fields.async: true returns inter-write spacing to the model round trip. Sync handlers run strictly serially: a 19-edit batch becomes a 3.6 s pause.
fields.asyncRewake: true wakes the session on exit 2 so the advisory stderr reaches the model as a system reminder. Without it the breach is written to a stream nobody reads.
fields.command: The whole invocation as one shell command line, the one field every harness that loads the plugin keeps. The bare console script, because `python` resolves to the WindowsApps stub and to venvs without crapkit. No `if`: claude-hook skips a file whose suffix crapkit does not measure before it reads any config.
fields.timeout: 20 s against a measured max of 245.6 ms.
fields.statusMessage: What the transcript shows while it runs.
